topics.topic: How the fixed SQL table names should be supplied without unavailable config.persistence references
questions: Must the config.persistence references be removed in favor of the mandated fixed SQL names, or must a configuration import or constant providing those names be added to IMPORTS?
Must config and its persistence constants be added to IMPORTS, or must the CONFIG_REFERENCE note provide the literal table-name values without referring to unavailable config data?

judgement.why: This asks the same fixed-literal-table-name versus unavailable config import question already answered by P1, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Resolve the undeclared config reference in create_budget_schema
quotes: create_budget_schema: [CONFIG_REFERENCE] MUST idempotently create only the tables budget_versions (= config.persistence.budget_version_table_name) and section_plans (= config.persistence.section_plan_table_name), written as fixed names in the SQL text, with columns corresponding one-to-one to BudgetVersion and SectionPlan fields; version_id and plan_id are primary keys, (version_id, section_id) is unique, and nullable model fields remain nullable.
Use only the IMPORTS listed above plus required standard library imports.
precedent.why: The prompt explicitly requires the literal fixed table names in SQL and permits no unlisted config-module import.

topics.topic: Whether an allowed OPTIONS preflight terminates with 204 or continues through the body-size check
questions: Must an allowed OPTIONS preflight end immediately with its 204 response, or must it continue through the body-size check because it was not refused?

quotes: For every request the middleware MUST evaluate the checks below in the order they are written, and the order is a pipeline rather than a choice between alternatives: each check either produces the response named for it and ends the request there, or leaves the request untouched for the next check to evaluate.

answer an OPTIONS request carrying an Origin listed in settings.allowed_origins with a 204 preflight echoing the requested method and headers plus Vary Origin, together with the allow-origin and allow-credentials headers every allowed-origin response carries, and reject an unlisted origin with 403;
judgement.why: The allowed OPTIONS check produces the named 204 response and therefore ends the request before the body-size check.
